title: Last Title Left
reviewNotes: Preserved all positions, outcomes and teaching commentary. Marked the two explicitly independent rook conversions as independent alternatives in branch provenance, matching their existing prose. Original review retained in history.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to win from [music] this incredible position. You see, at first glance it seems like we can just get a queen, but this would actually be a massive blunder because black would promote in return with a check. The only move is king to G3 and this would lead to a checkmate in two moves. So, we have to restrain from getting the new queen and instead play the very precise bishop to F3 preparing to sacrifice the bishop for the newly born queen. But actually now black can promote this pawn and now stop the promotion of the white pawn. Or at least, that's what it seems like at first glance. But as it turns out, white can indeed still promote to a new queen. Because of course, if black does take this queen, now white is going to have rook to E1 check and open an attack on the queen. After the king moves, we would pick up the queen and still prevent the promotion of the other pawn. So, it might seem like white is just about to win this position, right? Well, not that fast. Black does have a surprising resource and he can promote the other pawn to a new queen with a check forcing white to sacrifice the bishop for the queen. But of course, the idea is not to take this bishop because this would allow white to win the [music] queen. No, the idea is to now capture the white queen in the corner. And at first glance this doesn't seem to make any sense. If we give a check, the rook is still defending the bishop, so the black king cannot take. If the black king was to go to F2, we could still pick up the queen and this would still be winning. But you see, black has found a cunning idea and has set up a trap. But before I show you this next move, don't forget that [music] you can now get the Fools Will Resign merch from the link in my bio, which may or may not add 100 Elo points to your rating. After king to H2, because now surprisingly, seemingly out of nowhere, we cannot take this queen because this would actually be a stalemate. The king and the pawns have no legal moves, but the king is not checkmated, so this is a draw. So, white cannot take this queen, but he cannot leave it on the board either, or this would still be a draw, and actually black would have a bit of counterplay. So, is black just out of the woods, and is this game going to be a draw? Well, not exactly. White has the very common precise bishop to e4. [music] This move is achieving three things at the same time. It is maintaining the attack on the queen, and is blocking the checks from the queen, meaning that if black just moves the queen, this is going to be a checkmate in one. But, if the queen takes the bishop, after the rook takes, this is going to be, obviously, a winning end game for white.
